editions.title: Alphabet sheds $500bn as AI spending doubts hit Big Tech and Intel crashes
editions.notification: Alphabet loses $500bn in a day as AI spending doubts spread; Intel slumps on weak PC outlook.
editions.intro:
Investor patience with AI spending cracked this week. Alphabet lost just over $500bn in value after its quarterly update showed AI summaries in search weighing on advertising, with free cash flow negative by over $9bn. Amazon's free cash flow also swung deeply negative and its shares fell in after-hours trading, while Microsoft's shares barely moved despite 19% revenue growth. A global tech sell-off was reported to be deepening as the Nikkei and Wall Street opened lower.

Intel was the sharpest casualty. Its shares fell by roughly a quarter after third-quarter client chip revenue dropped and the company guided fourth-quarter revenue and earnings below expectations, blaming a memory shortage that is squeezing PC demand. Intel expects the PC market to shrink 12% this year. Reddit, meanwhile, said search referrals had fallen sharply and it will move to a logged-in-only experience, a direct example of how AI search is reshaping traffic.

Crypto was hit by a major security failure. Binance said an attacker drained hot wallets, with the affected amount put at about $6.3bn, and it pledged to cover losses from its SAFU fund and company money. Separately, reports that Nvidia's chief executive had ties to a Singapore businesswoman suspected by US intelligence of helping Beijing are unverified and have been strongly denied by Nvidia. Dealmaking continued, with DoorDash agreeing to buy Instacart for about $17bn and the FCC approving Amazon's Globalstar acquisition.

top_stories.title: Alphabet loses $500bn as AI search fears hit shares
top_stories.summary: Alphabet fell almost 13% to a six-month low after AI summaries in search were blamed for weaker ad revenue, even though Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon also fell after-hours on negative free cash flow, while Microsoft held up better. The reaction shows investors increasingly questioning the payoff from heavy AI spending.

top_stories.title: Intel shares plunge after weak PC chip outlook
top_stories.summary: Intel shares fell almost a quarter after client revenue fell and fourth-quarter guidance missed estimates by a wide margin. Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan blamed memory shortages and supply constraints, and forecast the PC market shrinking 12% this year. The stock had more than doubled earlier this year, so the drop is steep.

top_stories.title: Binance hit by about $6.3bn crypto theft
top_stories.summary: Attackers drained Binance hot wallets, with the affected funds put at around $6.3bn, and Tether and Circle froze stablecoins to help. Binance says the likely entry point was a compromised engineer's laptop and has pledged to cover all customer losses. The SAFU reserve covers only a fraction of the amount, so company funds will carry much of the cost.

top_stories.title: Reddit moves to logged-in-only experience
top_stories.summary: Reddit will test a logged-in-only experience in select non-US markets from Q4, citing a drop of over a million search referrals a week. The CEO warned daily active users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 if the trend continues. Reddit still reported Q3 revenue up 53% to $895m.

top_stories.title: DoorDash to buy Instacart for $17bn
top_stories.summary: DoorDash has agreed to acquire rival Instacart at $65 per share, a 26% premium, with at least 75% in cash. The deal still needs regulatory and shareholder approval. It would consolidate two major US grocery and delivery players.

top_stories.summary: According to The Information, Nvidia is in talks to provide billions of dollars in credit guarantees for Nscale's West Virginia data centre, which Anthropic plans to use under a deal worth about $45bn. Nothing is signed and terms could change. It would make Nvidia chip supplier, equity investor and debt backer in one chain.

editions.title: Alphabet's $500bn slide and Intel's crash rattle tech
editions.notification: Alphabet loses $500bn as AI spending doubts spread; Intel and Binance also reel
editions.intro:
Wall Street's tech earnings season turned sharply on Thursday as investors questioned how much AI spending will pay off. Alphabet shed just over $500bn in value, falling almost 13% to a six-month low, after its quarterly update showed AI summaries in search weighing on advertising revenue. Profits fell 25% and free cash flow was negative by more than $9bn, even though Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon and Microsoft also reported strong top lines, but Amazon's free cash flow was deeply negative and its shares fell about 6% after hours, and a global tech sell-off was reported to be deepening.

Intel was the other major casualty. Its shares fell by almost a quarter after a steep drop in PC chip sales and a weak fourth-quarter forecast, with the chief executive blaming a memory-chip shortage and warning the PC market could shrink 12% this year. Datacentre and AI revenue rose 78%, but the company said it will likely not fully meet datacentre demand in the first half. Memory costs are a common thread, also hitting PC makers and smartphone shipments, which fell 20% in the third quarter.

Crypto and security stories dominated the rest of the day. Binance said an attacker drained hot wallets, with the affected funds now put at about $6.3bn; Tether and Circle froze stablecoin balances, and Binance has pledged to cover losses. Separately, a New York Times report alleging that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had ties to a Singapore businesswoman suspected of helping Beijing was met with Nvidia's denial. Several linked Nvidia items, including reported credit guarantees for Nscale, remain unconfirmed rumours.

top_stories.summary: Alphabet fell almost 13% to a six-month low after AI summaries in search weighed on ad revenue and profits dropped 25%. Amazon and Microsoft also reported, with Amazon's free cash flow deeply negative, fuelling worries about AI returns.

top_stories.summary: Intel fell by nearly a quarter after a weak fourth-quarter forecast and a steep drop in PC chip sales. It expects the PC market to shrink 12% this year and warned it will not fully meet datacentre demand early in 2027.

top_stories.summary: Attackers drained Binance hot wallets, reportedly via a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop. Tether and Circle froze balances, and Binance says it will cover all customer losses from its SAFU fund and company money.

top_stories.summary: The New York Times reports Jensen Huang had close ties with a Megaspeed director US intelligence suspects of helping Beijing. Nvidia says only ordinary commercial information was shared, and the claims rest on unnamed sources.

top_stories.summary: According to The Information, Nvidia is negotiating credit guarantees for Nscale's West Virginia data centre, which Anthropic plans to use under a deal worth about $45bn. Nothing is signed and terms could change.

top_stories.title: FCC clears Amazon's $11.5bn Globalstar deal
top_stories.summary: The FCC approved the transfer of mobile-satellite spectrum to Amazon, which needs it for a planned direct-to-device system. The deal is expected to close in 2027, creating a stronger rival to SpaceX and AST SpaceMobile.

top_stories.summary: Omdia says shipments fell to 254.7 million, the weakest third quarter since 2013, as device prices rise. Samsung and Apple held up best, while Chinese brands fell sharply.

editions.title: Binance hack, Alphabet rout and Intel slump rattle tech
editions.notification: Binance hit by a roughly $6.3bn crypto theft as Alphabet and Intel shares tumble on AI doubts.
editions.intro:
Markets and security were the dominant stories over the last 24 hours. Binance said an attacker drained its hot wallets, with the affected funds later put at about $6.3 billion. Tether and Circle froze significant stablecoin balances to help, and Binance has pledged to cover all losses from its SAFU fund and company money. The exchange blamed a likely entry point via a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, and withdrawals remain paused while it overhauls security. A crypto industry figure has said the bitcoin is probably unrecoverable, though that is an opinion rather than an official update.

Earnings reshaped the market mood. Alphabet lost just over $500bn in value after AI summaries in search weighed on ad revenue, even as Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon's free cash flow turned sharply negative and its shares fell in after-hours trading. Intel dropped almost a quarter of its value after PC chip sales fell, with its CEO warning the PC chip market could shrink 12% next year. Taken together, investors are increasingly questioning how much AI spending will pay back.

Nvidia was the subject of several reports. The Information says it is in talks to guarantee billions of dollars of debt for Nscale's West Virginia data centre, which Anthropic plans to use under a deal worth about $45 billion. Separately, a New York Times report alleges US intelligence suspected a Singapore executive of acting for Beijing and linked her to Jensen Huang; Nvidia and the Chinese embassy have denied wrongdoing, and the claims rest on unnamed sources.

top_stories.title: Binance hot wallets drained, roughly $6.3bn affected
top_stories.summary: Binance said an attacker drained hot wallets and later put the affected funds at about $6.3bn. Tether and Circle froze large stablecoin balances, and Binance has pledged to cover all losses while withdrawals stay paused for a security overhaul. The SAFU fund covers only about a sixth of the amount.

top_stories.title: Alphabet loses $500bn as AI search fears hit ads
top_stories.summary: Alphabet shares fell almost 13% to a six-month low after AI summaries weighed on search ad revenue and profits fell 25%. Google Cloud grew 103%, but free cash flow was negative. Amazon also fell after its results showed a $42bn negative free cash flow.

top_stories.title: Intel shares sink a quarter on PC chip slump
top_stories.summary: Intel fell almost a quarter after client computing revenue dropped and the CEO warned PC chip demand could shrink 12% next year. Datacenter and AI sales grew 78%, but supply constraints mean it may not fully meet datacenter demand in the first half.

top_stories.title: Nvidia reportedly weighs credit backing for Nscale deal
top_stories.summary: The Information reports Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions of dollars of debt for Nscale's 460MW West Virginia campus tied to Anthropic's $45bn compute deal. Nothing is signed, and the report comes as scrutiny of AI data centre financing grows.

top_stories.title: NYT links Jensen Huang to Megaspeed executive under suspicion
top_stories.summary: The New York Times reports Nvidia's chief executive had close ties with a Megaspeed director whom US intelligence suspects of acting for Beijing. There is no evidence Huang knew of the suspicions, Nvidia says the contacts were ordinary business, and the claims rest on unnamed sources.

top_stories.title: Data on 41,000 DHS staff leaked online
top_stories.summary: Personal details of more than 41,000 Department of Homeland Security staff, including immigration agents, were published after a group claimed access via Okta single sign-on. DHS says it is investigating, while Okta says it sees no evidence its systems were compromised.

top_stories.title: Reddit moves towards logged-in-only experience
top_stories.summary: Reddit's CEO said the platform is moving to a logged-in-only experience, with tests in select non-US markets from Q4. Falling search referrals prompted the change, and the company warned daily active uniques could drop by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 if trends continue.

A brief Digitimes report on 10-year DRAM deals by Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance is plausible given the memory shortage but lacks detail.

editions.title: Apple's touchscreen Mac, Samsung's record profit and AI chip deals
editions.notification: Apple finally adds touchscreen MacBook Pros, and Samsung posts a record $80.5bn quarter.
editions.intro:
Apple has broken its long refusal to put touchscreens on Macs. The new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models use OLED XDR displays with touch input, and they start at $2,899 and $3,399 respectively. Pre-orders are open and shipping begins on 6 November. The launch is the first big product news under new chief executive John Ternus, and it comes with a premium price that buyers will notice.

The chip and memory sector dominated the day. Samsung reported a record third-quarter operating profit of KRW 107.4 trillion (about $80.5bn), driven by memory chips for AI data centres. Its executives said memory shortages will worsen in 2027 and persist into 2028, with long-term agreements covering 60 to 70% of capacity. Shares nonetheless slid, because profits narrowly missed some estimates and little was said about shareholder returns. Oracle, meanwhile, outlined a multi-vendor AI infrastructure push, deploying Nvidia Vera Rubin systems, AMD MI455X GPUs and Google TPUs from 2027.

On the deal front, the FCC approved Amazon's $11.5bn purchase of Globalstar, which strengthens Amazon's direct-to-device satellite ambitions and puts pressure on AST SpaceMobile. Separately, reports say OpenAI is considering buying Google TPUs, and Anthropic is weighing a retail tranche of up to 20% in its IPO. Both remain unconfirmed.

top_stories.title: Apple launches touchscreen MacBook Pro starting at $2,899
top_stories.summary: Apple has launched 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros with OLED touch displays, its first touchscreen Macs. Pre-orders are open and shipping starts 6 November. The premium pricing is $400 above the current equivalent model.

top_stories.title: Samsung posts record $80.5bn quarterly operating profit
top_stories.summary: Samsung's chip division drove a record KRW 107.4 trillion operating profit on AI memory demand. The smartphone unit posted a loss due to higher memory costs, and capex is set at KRW 84.4 trillion this year.

top_stories.title: Samsung warns memory shortages will last into 2028
top_stories.summary: Samsung says HBM4 supply for 2027 is sold out and tight memory supply will persist into 2028. Long-term agreements with 10 major customers cover 60 to 70% of its capacity.

top_stories.title: Samsung shares fall on thin investor-return detail
top_stories.summary: Samsung shares slid after quarterly profits fell just short of estimates. Investors got a bullish outlook but little detail on shareholder payouts.

top_stories.title: Oracle lines up Nvidia, AMD, Intel and Google chips
top_stories.summary: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure outlined a multi-vendor AI build-out, including Nvidia Vera Rubin, AMD MI455X and Intel Diamond Rapids. It will also be the first hyperscaler outside Google to deploy Google TPUs, from 2027.

top_stories.title: FCC clears Amazon's $11.5bn Globalstar acquisition
top_stories.summary: The FCC approved the deal, including transfer of key mobile-satellite spectrum, to support Amazon's planned direct-to-device system. Closing is expected in 2027, and AST SpaceMobile shares slipped overnight.

top_stories.title: Anthropic may reserve up to 20% of IPO for retail
top_stories.summary: Bloomberg reports Anthropic is considering a 15% to 20% retail allocation, with JPMorgan leading. The S-1 also shows heavy compute commitments and an 85% gross margin, and Senator Warren has raised questions.

rumour_watch.note: OpenAI buying Google TPUs is only reported, with no volume, price or timing confirmed; treat as unverified and not a reason to sell Nvidia on its own.
Retail allocation comes from Bloomberg citing sources and the S-1 only allows for it, so it is credible but not final.
Distillation claims against DeepSeek and Moonshot are unconfirmed and come from a single outlet, though Anthropic made similar accusations earlier.
A cheaper Switch 2 Lite is speculation built on a chip-process report from a single outlet, with no Nintendo comment.

editions.title: Apple readies touchscreen MacBook Pro as Anthropic prospectus lands
editions.notification: Apple may finally put touch on the Mac this Wednesday, and Anthropic's IPO filing shows a $80.7bn half-year loss.
editions.intro:
Apple dominates the day's agenda. Reports citing Bloomberg's Mark Gurman say Apple will unveil redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models on Wednesday 28 October, with touch-enabled OLED displays, which would be the first touchscreen Mac and a reversal of a long-held stance. Touchscreen models are reportedly premium additions, with the 14-inch starting at $2,899. Apple has also confirmed a refreshed iMac and entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, priced from $1,499 and $1,999, and it is acknowledging a small number of hinge-related screen failures on its $2,000 iPhone Duo, which has prompted questions about quality control on the new foldable.

The biggest financial story is Anthropic's public filing ahead of a US listing. The 335-page document shows a $80.7bn loss for the first half of 2026 on $16.2bn of revenue, roughly double its full-year 2025 loss, alongside heavy customer concentration and large data-centre costs. Valuations of $2 trillion or more are being discussed. Infrastructure news reinforced the AI chip story: Oracle plans to offer Google TPUs through its cloud from 2027, and OpenAI is reportedly considering buying TPUs, a move that would pressure Nvidia's position, although Nvidia is also gaining multi-gigawatt Vera Rubin deployments at Oracle.

Elsewhere, China's tech-heavy stocks have fallen sharply, with the STAR 50 down around 40% since June, while India's Jio Platforms rose 21% on its market debut. Microsoft is offering voluntary exit packages to roughly 60,000 staff, and it reports earnings this week.

top_stories.title: Apple set to unveil touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro on Wednesday
top_stories.summary: Citing Bloomberg, reports say Apple will show redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros with touch-enabled OLED screens on 28 October. If confirmed, it would be the first touchscreen Mac and a clear break from Apple's previous position.

top_stories.title: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals $80.7bn half-year loss
top_stories.summary: The 335-page prospectus shows $16.2bn in revenue and an $80.7bn loss in the first half of 2026, with heavy customer concentration and data-centre costs. Expected valuation is $2 trillion or more, making it a major test for AI listings.

top_stories.title: Oracle brings multiple AI chip vendors into one cloud
top_stories.summary: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is deploying Nvidia Vera Rubin, AMD MI455X, Intel Diamond Rapids and Google TPUs from 2027. The move positions Oracle as a multi-vendor AI infrastructure hub and is a notable first for TPUs outside Google's own cloud.

top_stories.title: OpenAI reportedly plans to buy Google TPUs
top_stories.summary: According to The Information, OpenAI intends to buy Google's AI chips, deepening ties despite rivalry. Terms are undisclosed, but the move could pressure Nvidia's dominance in AI accelerators.

top_stories.title: Jio shares jump 21% on India market debut
top_stories.summary: Jio Platforms opened at ₹1,358 against a ₹1,119 IPO price, valuing it at about $131.9bn. The listing is one of India's largest and makes it the country's second most valuable listed company after Reliance.

top_stories.title: Chinese tech markets lose trillions in AI race
top_stories.summary: The STAR 50 is down about 40% since June and Bloomberg estimates $2.4tn has been wiped from Chinese stocks since May. Weak profits, soft consumer demand and fears of further US tech bans are cited, with the Party plenum next in focus.

top_stories.title: Apple acknowledges iPhone Duo screen failures
top_stories.summary: Apple says a small number of its $2,000 foldable iPhone Duo have inner-display problems, which iFixit links to the hinge. Customers are being directed to AppleCare for replacements, though the company has not disclosed the cause.

rumour_watch.note: Credible: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman is a strong source, and a follow-up report puts pricing and an invitation-only hands-on in Los Angeles on the same date, so the launch looks likely.
Weak: a one-line Digitimes headline with no detail on volumes or timing; treat as unconfirmed until a second source appears.
Low credibility: a feed summary at 20% citing a secondhand report of relaxed quality checks and a refused warranty claim, with no Apple response.
Moderately credible: The Information is well-sourced, and OpenAI has posted a TPU-optimisation job, though financial terms are unknown.

editions.title: Microsoft's 60,000 buyout, Meta's $95bn raise and iPhone Duo woes
editions.notification: Microsoft reportedly offers buyouts to about a quarter of its workforce as Apple's iPhone Duo faces screen questions.
editions.intro:
Microsoft dominated the day's business news. Reports say it is offering voluntary exit packages to roughly 60,000 staff, about a quarter of its workforce, in the US, UK, India and Canada. The company frames it as choice and flexibility, following an April retirement offer and July layoffs, and it reports earnings later this week. The move fits a wider Big Tech pattern of redirecting spending towards AI.

Apple's new foldable, the iPhone Duo, had a rougher start. Apple acknowledged that a small number of units have inner-display problems, and it is directing affected customers to AppleCare for replacements. iFixit's teardown points to the hinge as a possible cause, though it has not confirmed one. Apple's Mac and iPad launches are also expected this week, with reports of touch-enabled OLED MacBook Pros on Wednesday.

On the AI front, Meta is reported to be planning a $95bn stock offering to fund its AI build-out, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom named as cornerstone investors. Anthropic's IPO paperwork revealed a $80.7bn first-half loss on $16.2bn revenue, while OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra at half the API price of its predecessor and claimed several science breakthroughs. Chinese tech stocks, meanwhile, have lost an estimated $2.4tn since May.

top_stories.title: Microsoft reportedly offers buyouts to about 60,000 staff
top_stories.summary: Reports say Microsoft is preparing voluntary exit offers covering around a quarter of its workforce in the US, UK, India and Canada. The company frames it as a choice for staff, alongside reskilling, and it follows earlier cuts this year. The move reflects a wider shift of spending towards AI.

top_stories.title: Meta reportedly plans $95bn stock offering for AI
top_stories.summary: The Financial Times reports Meta plans a $95bn stock offering to finance its AI expansion, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom as cornerstone investors. Only the headline and summary were available, so size and terms remain unconfirmed. If confirmed, it would be a very large equity raise.

top_stories.title: Apple acknowledges iPhone Duo inner-display issue
top_stories.summary: Apple said a small number of iPhone Duo units have an inner display problem, after social media reports of screen failures. Apple says the number of affected units does not appear large. iFixit's teardown links the failures to the hinge, though the cause is not confirmed.

top_stories.title: Anthropic's IPO filing shows heavy losses
top_stories.summary: Anthropic's 335-page filing reports an $80.7bn loss in the first half of the year on $16.2bn revenue. It is widely expected to be valued at $2 trillion or more. The filing also highlights customer concentration and large data-centre costs.

top_stories.title: Touch-screen OLED MacBook Pro reportedly due Wednesday
top_stories.summary: Reports citing Bloomberg's Mark Gurman say Apple will unveil redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros with touch OLED displays on 28 October. It would be the first touchscreen Mac and reverse Apple's long-held stance. The machines are reported to keep M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

top_stories.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra at half the price
top_stories.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra costs $1 per million input tokens and $5 for output, half of GPT-5.6 Terra. Artificial Analysis calls it a new benchmark for intelligence per dollar. OpenAI says it meets its Critical cybersecurity threshold.

top_stories.title: Chinese tech markets shed trillions amid AI rivalry
top_stories.summary: The STAR 50 index is reported down about 40% since June, and Bloomberg estimates $2.4tn has been wiped from Chinese stocks since May. Analysts cite weak profits, soft consumer demand and fears of further US tech bans. Attention is on the upcoming Communist Party plenum.

rumour_watch.note: Sourced to the Financial Times, but only the headline and summary were available, so the size and cornerstone investors are unverified.
Credible: based on Bloomberg's Mark Gurman with invitations reportedly sent, and a 28 October date is consistent across reports.
Highly credible: Bloomberg and CNN reporting, and a Microsoft memo from its chief people officer matches the framing.
Weak: a single Reddit post with no independent evidence, and Apple's position is secondhand.

stocks_to_watch.note: Buyout plans could cut costs, but the company's earnings this week will show the wider picture.

stocks_to_watch.note: Duo screen concerns weigh, while expected Mac and iPad launches could support sentiment.

stocks_to_watch.name: Nvidia

stocks_to_watch.name: Samsung Electronics
stocks_to_watch.note: Benefits from AI memory demand, but faces cuts to budget Galaxy A production and an India sales slump.

stocks_to_watch.note: Hacking incident and trading-loss compensation pressure the company.

in_brief.line: Gadgets 360 reports Apple has acknowledged iPhone Duo inner-display failures, though details remain unclear.
Intel's RPL-NEXT driver hints at Raptor Lake Next desktop chips reusing LGA-1700 boards, with no pricing yet.
ETNews reports Samsung may cut budget Galaxy A output by 20% in Q4 as memory costs rise; Samsung has not confirmed.
Counterpoint says India's smartphone shipments fell 20% in Q3, the weakest quarter in a decade, as memory prices bite.
GMO Internet's Onamae.com Desktop Cloud was compromised, with unauthorised trades and a refused ransom demand.
Apple released iOS 27.2 with recall-enabled Siri AI, FaceTime dual-camera support and iPhone Duo updates.
OpenAI claims its internal model disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis, with independent experts leading the review.
Virgin Galactic delays its first commercial Delta flight to early Q2 2027; SPCE shares eased after hours.

Finance.title: Alphabet's record fall and the Binance hack roil markets
Finance.notification: Alphabet shares suffer their worst-ever day, wiping out about half a trillion dollars
Finance.summary:
Alphabet's worst-ever single-day fall dominated markets, with shares down more than 12% and roughly half a trillion dollars of value lost after third-quarter revenue missed expectations despite cloud growth. Investors are increasingly worried that AI is eroding the company's search earnings. The sell-off spread to Amazon, which fell after heavy AI spending and a slower e-commerce business, and to Intel, leaving the Nasdaq weaker.

Crypto was also under pressure after Binance reported a security breach involving about $6.3bn, widely described as the largest crypto theft on record. Withdrawals have been halted, and reports suggest the stolen bitcoin may be gone, hitting sentiment towards listed crypto names such as Coinbase and Strategy.

Across Asia, the tech selloff hit chipmakers and the Nikkei, which closed down 2.12%, while the KOSPI fell 3.48%. The Bank of Japan held rates at 1.25% but signalled further tightening, and the yen firmed.

highlights.label: US
highlights.text: Amazon fell after heavy AI capex plans of about $220bn for 2026, despite AWS growth of 39% and a bullish $1trn ambition for the cloud unit.

highlights.label: UK
highlights.text: BP posted record profits on high fuel prices and is using the windfall to pay down debt, while AstraZeneca beat expectations on cancer drugs.

highlights.label: Europe
highlights.text: France's economy unexpectedly contracted in the third quarter as exports slumped, raising questions for the eurozone outlook.

highlights.label: Asia
highlights.text: The KOSPI closed down 3.48% as SK Hynix fell 7.08%, while the Nikkei lost 2.12% on AI-linked tech worries.

highlights.label: Markets
highlights.text: Binance halted withdrawals after a breach it says affects about $6.3bn, with reports saying around $3bn has been frozen so far.

highlights.label: Budget
highlights.text: Chancellor John Healey's Budget raised the small business rates threshold, but business groups say it does little to stop high street decline.

points.text: Amazon's Q3 capex topped $77bn, well above estimates, while e-commerce growth was its slowest in three years.
Volkswagen posted a €5.86bn Q3 operating loss and plans around 100,000 job cuts and possible plant closures.
Tesco agreed to sell its Czech and Slovak businesses to Ahold Delhaize for about £1.5bn, exiting another international market.
Poundland has filed a notice of intent to appoint administrators, putting around 12,000 jobs at risk.
BoJ kept rates at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote, with one member pushing for 1.50%, and markets expect a December hike.
About 91% of Monte dei Paschi voters rejected defence measures against Intesa Sanpaolo's takeover bid.

World.title: Spain train crash, US midterms and Iran war dominate
World.notification: Spain's rail disaster toll passes 68 as questions turn to the government's safety record.
World.summary:
The deadliest story in this set is the high-speed train collision in central Spain, which killed at least 68 people and injured dozens more. The first findings suggest a train was ordered to proceed in error after a control-system failure, renewing questions over rail safety after January's crash on the same line. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has promised answers, and the disaster is now reshaping a snap election due next month.

In the US, the midterms are four days away. Democrats lead in national polling, Donald Trump has cancelled weekend rallies in Kansas and Iowa, and the Justice Department's subpoenas in the Alaska Senate race have added a legal dimension. Foreign policy is a live issue: the Iran war has disrupted Gulf shipping, Brent crude has traded above $117 a barrel, and a senator has called reported plans to restart the offensive "insane". Alphabet's record one-day fall of about 12%, which wiped roughly $500bn off its value, has deepened fears that AI spending may not pay off.

Elsewhere, Israel's inconclusive election leaves Benjamin Netanyahu without a clear route to a majority, while in the UK the Budget's bank tax rise and Home Office migration tensions dominate. In Asia, the Bank of Japan held rates but signalled further hikes, which is supporting the yen.

highlights.label: US
highlights.text: Trump cancels Kansas and Iowa rallies for tele-rallies four days before the midterms; Alaska Senate race faces Justice Department subpoenas.

highlights.label: UK
highlights.text: Chancellor Healey's first Budget raises the bank tax and pledges a welfare cut; Home Secretary Mahmood faces criticism over asylum reform impacts.

highlights.label: Europe
highlights.text: Spain's snap election is reshaped by the rail crash, with opposition parties attacking the government over safety.

highlights.label: Asia
highlights.text: The Bank of Japan kept rates steady but signalled further hikes, lifting the yen and putting bank shares in focus.

highlights.label: Markets
highlights.text: Alphabet shares fell over 12% after results, its biggest one-day loss, while Microsoft rose more than 5%.

highlights.label: Oil
highlights.text: Brent topped $117 as Iran war disruption, mines in Hormuz and fears of renewed hostilities keep the market tight.

points.text: Healey promises a smaller welfare bill before the next election, with disability and NEET reviews due in November.
Ministers reportedly frustrated that Mahmood has not shared an assessment on asylum reform and homelessness.
UK defence offset rules will require foreign contractors with contracts over £50m to invest in British industry from April 2027.
Reports say Lagarde will step down early, triggering an ECB succession race as France heads toward its presidential vote.
EU states will release 42.6m barrels of reserves, roughly four days of consumption, with a costly winter for gas and diesel expected.
China expelled a record 33 Central Committee members, with many seats empty as Xi tightens control ahead of the 2027 Party Congress.

Tech.title: AI spending doubts hit Big Tech and chip stocks
Tech.notification: Alphabet loses $500bn in a day as investors question the cost of AI spending
Tech.summary:
Investor worries about the payoff from huge AI spending dominated tech today. Alphabet lost just over $500bn in value after its results showed AI summaries in search weighing on advertising, with free cash flow negative and profits down 25%, even as Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon also fell after heavy spending pushed free cash flow negative, and a global tech sell-off was reported as US earnings stoked fears.

The chip sector felt the strain too. Intel shares fell by about a quarter after a weak PC chip outlook, which it blamed on memory shortages and falling PC demand, while Nvidia faced reports of ties between its chief executive and a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence of helping route chips to China. Nvidia's reported credit guarantees for Nscale, tied to an Anthropic compute deal, added to concerns about how the AI build-out is financed.

Elsewhere, Binance suffered a hack that drained about $6.3 billion in crypto from hot wallets, with Binance pledging to cover customer losses. Reddit's move to logged-in-only access, prompted by falling search referrals from Google, added to the picture of AI search reshaping online traffic.

highlights.label: Binance hack
highlights.text: About $6.3bn in crypto drained from hot wallets; Tether and Circle froze balances and Binance pledged to cover losses.

highlights.label: Intel
highlights.text: Shares fell by almost a quarter after a weak Q4 forecast; Intel expects the PC market to shrink 12% this year.

highlights.label: Samsung
highlights.text: Record Q3 operating profit of 107.44 trillion won, driven by chips, while devices made a loss.

points.text: Nadella said Copilot daily users rose nearly 50% in the quarter and more than fivefold year on year.
Jassy said AWS could reach a trillion-dollar scale; AWS grew 39.3% to just under $46bn in Q3.
Nvidia will invest $3bn in Meta's share offering and expand work on AI agent systems.
Anthropic made up 34.5% of SpaceX's Q3 revenue, per Bloomberg, making it bigger than the US government as a client.
Murata plans ¥1 trillion of investment over five years to more than double MLCC sales for AI data centres.
Global smartphone shipments fell 20% in Q3, the weakest third quarter since 2013, Omdia said.

Fashion.title: Couture comeback and Gucci's store reboot lead luxury news
Fashion.notification: Versace is returning to haute couture in 2027, with Hermès and Celine also moving that way
Fashion.summary:
Luxury houses are leaning into exclusivity. Versace will bring back Atelier Versace couture in January 2027, with Pieter Mulier's first full runway show for the brand, a year after Prada Group's roughly €1.25 billion acquisition. Hermès is also set to debut couture that month, and Celine is reportedly developing a couture offer. Analysts say couture supports exclusivity and pricing, a theme that fits the sector's focus on wealthy, high-spending clients.

Retail is being reshaped too. Gucci has opened a redesigned four-floor store on Avenue Montaigne in Paris, the first use of a new concept that will roll out to London, Shanghai and Chengdu by year-end. CEO Francesca Bellettini says it is built to outlast any single creative director, amid rapid turnover in the brand's creative leadership and as Kering's turnaround under Luca de Meo closes underperforming stores.

Elsewhere, Puig set a target of €8 billion in annual sales by 2032, and Adidas's strong third quarter, with direct-to-consumer sales up 17%, shows sportswear is also a growth engine. The RealReal reported revenue up 19%.

highlights.label: Couture
highlights.text: Versace returns to haute couture in January 2027 under Pieter Mulier; Hermès is set to debut and Celine is reportedly developing one.

highlights.label: Gucci
highlights.text: A redesigned Avenue Montaigne store opens as the template for a rollout to London, Shanghai and Chengdu by year-end.

highlights.label: Adidas
highlights.text: Q3 sales hit a record €7.3 billion, with operating profit up 37%; direct-to-consumer sales rose 17%.

highlights.label: Resale
highlights.text: The RealReal's Q3 revenue rose 19% to $206 million and it raised full-year guidance.

points.text: Luxury brands are competing hard for top salespeople, some earning around a million dollars a year.
Volkswagen is not a fashion story, but it is a reminder of the premium carmakers' China and cost pressures.
